findings.title: JADEPUFFER: Agentic ransomware for automated database extortion
findings.summary_md: Sysdig Threat Research Team's original report by Michael Clark, published July 1, 2026, five days before this story's first sighting. It documents the full operation: initial access to an internet-facing Langflow host via CVE-2025-3248, parallel harvesting of LLM provider and cloud credentials, MinIO enumeration with the minioadmin:minioadmin default pair, a crontab beaconing to 45.131.66[.]106:4444 every 30 minutes, and the pivot to a production MySQL and Alibaba Nacos server. Sysdig assesses the operator as an agentic threat actor whose entire extortion lifecycle ran through an LLM, with payloads that self-narrate and corrected a failed bcrypt backdoor insert within 31 seconds.

findings.title: Unsafe at Any Speed: Abusing Python Exec for Unauth RCE in Langflow AI
findings.summary_md: The original researcher disclosure by Naveen Sunkavally, published April 9, 2025, the same day a third-party public exploit appeared. It details the unauthenticated Python exec injection in Langflow's /api/v1/validate/code endpoint, reported to Langflow on February 22, 2025 and fixed by pull request #6911 merged March 5, 2025. Censys showed 500+ internet-exposed Langflow instances at disclosure time, and the patch in Langflow 1.3.0 puts the vulnerable endpoint behind authentication.

findings.title: CISA adds Langflow Missing Authentication Vulnerability (CVE-2025-3248) to KEV
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2025-3248, listed as Langflow Missing Authentication Vulnerability, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog on May 5, 2025 with a federal remediation due date of May 26, 2025. KEV listing requires evidence of in-the-wild exploitation, placing confirmed abuse of the flaw more than a year before the JADEPUFFER report. The addition date is confirmed in the KEV table on the NVD detail page.

findings.title: NVD entry for CVE-2025-3248 published
findings.summary_md: The NVD record for CVE-2025-3248 was published April 7, 2025 with VulnCheck as CNA and a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.8. It describes code injection in Langflow versions prior to 1.3.0 through the /api/v1/validate/code endpoint, letting a remote unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code, and references the Horizon3 disclosure and the Langflow 1.3.0 patch release.

findings.title: Langflow 1.3.0 release
findings.summary_md: The Langflow 1.3.0 release, published on GitHub March 31, 2025 (21:25:09 UTC per the GitHub API), is the patched release that closed CVE-2025-3248. Any Langflow deployment older than 1.3.0 remains exploitable, and the vulnerable code dates back roughly two years of releases according to Horizon3's testing. This is the concrete upgrade target defenders needed more than a year before JADEPUFFER put the flaw to work.
